concerns.text: FR-007 defines a runtime constraint (≤ 6 hours) but lacks a verifiable test procedure. 'Parallel processing where feasible' is non-deterministic. To be verifiable, the FR must specify the exact runner environment (e.g., 'GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest with 2 vCPUs') and the exact input set (e.g., '5 snapshots of 1024³ grid, factors 2,4,8,16') against which the 6h limit is measured. Without fixed inputs and environment, the constraint cannot be pass/fail tested.

FR-001 requires memory usage to be measured via '/proc/self/status RSS field'. This is Linux-specific and not verifiable on non-Linux runners (e.g., macOS/Windows in local dev or other CI). The requirement must be generalized to 'OS-agnostic memory accounting' or explicitly mandate a Linux-only execution environment to be verifiable across all intended contexts.

SC-004 states runtime is 'measured against the prescribed time limit of the GitHub Actions free-tier runner'. This is ambiguous and unmeasurable. The 'free-tier' has variable resources (2-core vs 4-core, burst limits). The SC must define the specific runner label (e.g., 'ubuntu-latest') and the exact dataset configuration (e.g., 'N=5, grid=1024³') to establish a reproducible baseline for the 6-hour limit.

SC-005 requires memory peak usage to be 'measured against a constrained RAM limit of the runner environment'. It fails to state the specific limit value (e.g., 7GB as mentioned in FR-001) or the specific runner configuration. A success criterion must state the threshold explicitly (e.g., 'Peak RSS ≤ 7000 MB') to be measurable.
